summary.short: Bill text that would amend Colorado Revised Statutes 6-1-1701 to 6-1-1707 to govern developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems making consequential decisions, mainly to avoid algorithmic discrimination. Most duties apply from January 1, 2027; the attorney general enforces them.
summary.long: Amends Part 17 of Article 1 of Title 6, Colorado Revised Statutes (sections 6-1-1701 to 6-1-1707), on high-risk artificial intelligence systems used in consequential decisions about consumers, such as employment, lending, housing, health care and insurance. From January 1, 2027, developers must give deployers documentation and statements of intended and known harmful uses, and keep records for at least three years. Deployers must adopt a risk management policy and program, complete impact assessments before first deployment and annually, and review systems yearly for algorithmic discrimination. From May 1, 2026, deployers must give consumers a pre-decision statement and, after an adverse decision, a notice within thirty days with an opportunity to correct data and appeal. AI systems interacting with consumers must be disclosed as AI from January 1, 2027. Exemptions cover small deployers, recruitment-only uses and systems that are not the principal basis of decisions. The attorney general has exclusive enforcement authority from January 1, 2027; violations are unfair trade practices, and an affirmative defense is available for curable violations cured within seven days. The act takes effect ninety days after adjournment, subject to referendum.

notes: Amending bill: changed wording is shown in capitals, but struck wording is kept in the text without strike markup, so some passages mix deleted and new wording (e.g., 6-1-1703(6)(a)(I) fewer than fifty FIVE HUNDRED). Dates conflict: several duties start MAY 1, 2026 (6-1-1703(4)(a)-(b)), 6-1-1703(9)(b) reads February 1, 2026 JANUARY 1, 2027, and most duties start January 1, 2027. Two separate employee-count tiers appear, in 6-1-1703(6)(a) and (6.3)(c). Section 3 repeals 6-1-1703(7), yet the text of (7) remains and refers to subsection (8). Some cross-references point to subsections not reproduced here (6-1-1703(3)(d), (3)(e); 6-1-1702(2)(d)). 6-1-1701(11)(a) is cut off after 'a factor that:'. 6-1-1706(3)(b)(III) is garbled ('if HAS designated'). The enacting act amended by these sections is not named in this text.
